newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary mobile phone firm to tap mkts for $170 mln.
newsitem.headline: Hungary mobile phone firm to tap mkts for $170 mln.

text.p: Hungarian mobile telephone service firm Westel 900 GSM Rt plans to tap markets for $170 million soon, daily newspaper Nepszava said on Saturday.
Citibank and Bank of America were mandated to organise a consortium of commercial banks, the newspaper said, without saying for what the loan is to be used.
The mobile telephone company's CEO said in late October that Westel 900 has invested 35 billion forints in Hungary and plans to spend the same amount for development by 2000.
Westel 900 is owned by the Hungarian telecommunications giant Matav, U.S. West and the International Finance Corp (IFC). -- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327-4040
